messages.subject: Plot options for gl.spatial.autoCorr
parts:
Hi folks,
I've recently been using the gl.spatial.autoCorr function - a fairly new addition to dartR's functionality - but I would like to add a title to some of the plots it produces, increase the x and y axes font sizes, etc. I can save the output of the function to a dataframe, and could with a bit of effort use the relevant columns to produce my own plot, but do you have any conveniently available code that would enable the current plot format to be reproduced as either a standard R plot or ggplot2 plot? There seem to be a number of dartR functions where there the options available to customize the plots produced are quite limited.

Thanks,
Peter

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Plot options for gl.spatial.autoCorr
parts:
Hi Peter,

Please find below some code for formatting plots in dartR. We will work in a tutorial about how to format plots, choose colors etc. 

library(dartR)
library(ggthemes)

test <- platypus.gl
# running the function with save2tmp = TRUE to save the plot and tables in
# the temporal directory
autocor <- gl.spatial.autoCorr(test,save2tmp = TRUE)
# listing the plots and tables in tempdir
gl.list.reports()
# choosing the plot or table to retrieve
res <- gl.print.reports(1)
# selecting colors
PopColours <- gl.select.colors(test,library =  "brewer",palette = "Set3",)

res+
  # changing theme
  theme_dark() +
  # add a title
  ggtitle("Spatial autocorrelation") +
  #increase title font
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 16)) +
    # increase the x and y axes font sizes
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16)) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16)) 

Cheers,
Luis
